The test image shows tomato leaves with a distinctive **silvery/bronze discoloration** across the leaf surface, small dark flecks/spots, and some leaf curling on the right side. The silvery-bronze sheen covering the whole leaf is the dominant feature.

This strongly suggests **Tomato_Spotted_Wilt_Virus** — bronzing/silvering of leaves is its hallmark symptom. Let me confirm with a reference image.

The reference image shows TSWV at a whole-plant scale (wilting/collapse), while the test image shows an earlier/closer view. But the **silvery-bronze leaf discoloration with dark flecks** in the test image is the classic early-stage TSWV bronzing symptom — no other class in the list produces this characteristic metallic silver sheen across leaf surfaces.
